About This Dashboard

This dashboard provides a comprehensive view of IT engineering team performance based on ServiceNow incident data and work note activity.

How to use:

  • Use the date filter (From / To) to focus on a specific time period, then click Apply Filter. All charts update instantly.
  • Click the (i) button on any chart section to learn what that chart shows and how to read it.
  • Charts with engineer selectors let you filter which engineers are displayed.
  • Hover over any chart element for detailed values.

How hours are calculated:

Estimated hours = number of work notes x 20 minutes. Each time an engineer writes a work note or comment on a ticket, we estimate ~20 minutes of effort. This is an approximation, not time tracking.

Data Filters Applied:

  • Cancelled tickets (state=8) are excluded
  • Bot-created tickets (Zabbix Monitoring, Snow Sevone API) are excluded
  • Bot work notes (zbxincident) are excluded from activity counts

Data source: talapparel.service-now.com — Incidents + Work Notes (sys_journal_field)
Monthly Performance Trend VOLUME + MTTR i

Monthly Performance Trend

Shows how incident volume and resolution speed change over time.

  • Blue bars (left axis): Number of new incidents created each month
  • Red line (right axis): Median MTTR (Mean Time To Resolve) in hours — the midpoint resolution time for resolved tickets that month
  • Green dotted line (right axis): Median first response time in hours — how quickly an engineer writes the first work note after ticket creation

How to read: Ideally, bars stay stable or decrease while lines trend downward, meaning the team handles the same (or more) volume faster.

MTTR = resolved_at minus created_on. Response = first work note minus created_on. Median is used instead of average to avoid distortion from outliers.
Ticket Trend NEW vs RESOLVED i

Ticket Trend (New vs Resolved)

Tracks whether the team is keeping up with incoming work or falling behind.

  • Red bars: New incidents created that month
  • Green bars: Incidents resolved that month
  • Yellow line: Running backlog — cumulative difference between new and resolved. If green > red, the line drops (backlog shrinking). If red > green, the line rises (backlog growing).

How to read: Green bars should consistently match or exceed red bars. A rising yellow line is a warning sign that the team needs more capacity or prioritization.
Incident Distribution by Application TREEMAP i

Incident Distribution by Application

Shows which applications/systems generate the most incidents (top 20).

  • Box size: Proportional to the number of incidents for that application
  • Label: Application name, count, and percentage of total

How to read: The largest boxes are your highest-volume applications. Use this to identify systems that may need investment, dedicated support, or root-cause analysis.

Application = ServiceNow incident subcategory field. Tickets without a subcategory show as "(Unclassified)".
Engineering Workload — Tickets UNIQUE TICKETS / MONTH i

Engineering Workload — Tickets

Shows how many unique tickets each engineer worked on per month.

  • Each color: Represents one engineer (top 12 by volume, or filtered selection)
  • Bar height: Number of distinct tickets that engineer wrote at least one work note on
  • Stacked total: Combined ticket touches across selected engineers

How to read: Compare relative contributions month-over-month. A sudden drop for one engineer may indicate leave, reassignment, or workload shift. Use the engineer selector to focus on specific people.

A ticket is counted once per engineer per month, even if the engineer wrote multiple notes on it.
Engineering Workload — Hours ESTIMATED HOURS / MONTH i

Engineering Workload — Hours

Estimated time each engineer spent on incidents per month.

  • Each color: Represents one engineer
  • Bar height: Estimated hours = work notes count × 20 minutes

How hours are calculated: Every time an engineer writes a work note or comment on a ticket, we estimate ~20 minutes of effort. This is a practical approximation since ServiceNow does not track actual time spent. An engineer with 90 work notes in a month = 90 × 20 min = 30 estimated hours.

How to read: Use this to gauge relative workload distribution. If one engineer's bar is consistently tall, they may be overloaded. Use the selector to compare specific engineers.

This is an estimate, not actual time tracking. Real effort per note varies by complexity.
Engineer vs Application — Tickets HEATMAP i

Engineer vs Application — Tickets

A matrix showing how many unique tickets each engineer touched for each application.

  • Rows: Engineers (sorted by total tickets, highest at top)
  • Columns: Applications (sorted by total tickets, highest at left)
  • Cell color & number: Darker/higher = more tickets. The number shows the exact count.

How to read: Identify who specializes in which application. Bright cells = high involvement. Use this to understand team coverage and spot single points of failure (one person handling all tickets for an app).

Use the engineer selector (hold Ctrl/Cmd to multi-select) to focus on specific people. Top 20 apps shown.
Engineer vs Application — Hours HEATMAP i

Engineer vs Application — Hours

Same matrix as above, but showing estimated hours instead of ticket count.

  • Cell value: Estimated hours = work notes on that app × 20 min / 60
  • Color intensity: Purple to yellow gradient — brighter = more hours invested

How to read: An engineer may touch many tickets briefly (high ticket count, low hours) or few tickets deeply (low count, high hours). Compare this with the Tickets heatmap to understand depth vs breadth of involvement.

Hours = work notes × 20 minutes. This is an approximation, not actual time tracking.
Activity Patterns WHEN ENGINEERS WORK i

Activity Patterns

Shows when engineers are active — by day of week and hour of day (Bangkok time, UTC+7).

  • Rows: Days of the week (Monday at top, Sunday at bottom)
  • Columns: Hours of the day (00:00 to 23:00)
  • Cell color: Brighter = more work notes written at that time

How to read: Dark cells = low activity. Bright green/blue = peak activity. Use the dropdown to view patterns for a specific engineer or the whole team. Look for after-hours work, weekend activity, or coverage gaps.

Times are converted from ServiceNow UTC timestamps to Bangkok timezone (UTC+7).
Engineer Productivity Map BUBBLE i

Engineer Productivity Map

Plots each engineer as a bubble to visualize their overall workload profile (top 15).

  • X-axis (horizontal): Total unique tickets touched
  • Y-axis (vertical): Estimated total hours (notes × 20 min)
  • Bubble size: Number of unique applications the engineer worked on — bigger = broader coverage
  • Bubble color: Blue to red gradient based on ticket count — redder = more tickets

How to read: Top-right = high volume + high effort (heaviest contributors). Large bubbles = generalists working across many apps. Small bubbles in top-right = specialists handling many tickets in few apps. Bottom-left = lower activity.
Multi-Engineer Tickets by Application COLLABORATION / REASSIGNMENT i

Multi-Engineer Tickets

Identifies tickets that were worked on by 2 or more different engineers, grouped by application.

  • Red bars (left axis): Number of multi-engineer tickets for that application
  • Yellow line (right axis): Average number of engineers per ticket for that application

How to read: High bars may indicate:

  • Healthy collaboration — complex issues needing multiple specialists
  • Reassignment issues — tickets being bounced between people due to unclear ownership or routing

If the yellow line is high (3+), that app's tickets frequently require hand-offs. Consider dedicated ownership or better triage.

Based on distinct sys_created_by values in work notes per ticket. Only counts human engineers (bots excluded).
Engineer Scorecard TOP APPS PER ENGINEER i

Engineer Scorecard

A detailed table summarizing each engineer's activity across the selected period.

  • Tickets: Unique incidents the engineer wrote at least one work note on
  • Notes: Total work notes and comments written
  • Est. Hours: Notes × 20 minutes (effort estimate)
  • Apps: Number of unique applications (subcategories) worked on
  • Top Applications: The engineer's most-worked applications, showing ticket count and hours for each

How to read: Use Top 5 / Top 10 tabs to control how many apps are shown per engineer. Engineers are sorted by total tickets (highest first). This table is ideal for 1-on-1 reviews or workload discussions.
